newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec separatist says will quit in March.
newsitem.headline: Quebec separatist says will quit in March.

text.p: Michel Gauthier announced on Monday he was stepping down as leader of the opposition Bloc Quebecois, saying he had given a lacklustre performance as Quebec's top separatist at the federal level.

Gauthier failed to inspire separatists as effectively as his predecessor, Lucien Bouchard, who rallied separatists to near-victory in an October 1995 sovereignty referendum before leaving the Bloc to become premier of Quebec.

Gauthier said he would stay on until the next convention of the Bloc Quebecois, the official opposition in Canada's federal Parliament, in March. He said he would not be a candidate in the leadership race at that time.

"I think I had some problems with my leadership, and it's better for the Bloc to solve this problem," he told reporters after a 4-1/2-hour party caucus. "I think the party would be better served by a new leadership."
Some Bloc members had openly questioned his leadership.

In opinion polls, the Bloc had slipped under Gauthier's leadership to virtual parity with the ruling Liberals, who strenuously oppose the breakup of Canada but won only 20 Quebec seats in the 1993 federal elections compared to the Bloc's 53.
"He decided for the Bloc Quebecois and for the sovereignty of Quebec that it was better for him to step down," prominent Bloc member Francine Lalonde said after Gauthier's statement.
Separatists took 49.4 percent of the vote in the independence referendum. Polls since then have shown a gradual erosion in that support.
